subject: zoology
question_text: Define conjugation with reference to ciliates. Give two examples.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section, VSAQ chapter 16 'Locomotion & Reproduction' (book p.57, question 130). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are both STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for this card, not merely unrun; 'not checked' must never be read as 'checked and clean'. The mark split is this card's claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. MARKS: the VSAQ chapter header prints '2+2=4 MARKS', which is the blueprint's two 2-mark questions drawn from this unit, not 4 marks for one question; this card is authored at the Section A standard of 2 marks. APPEARANCES: the book prints [AP,TS-18] and [TS M-15]; the 2018 citation carries no month and is stored as the year alone for both boards. page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Definition
lines: Conjugation is the temporary union of two
senile ciliates of different mating types for
The two cells join at their oral surfaces and
each passes a migratory nucleus to the other.
steps.why: Three words carry the definition mark — temporary, two different mating types, and exchange of nuclear material — so all three must appear in the sentence.
common_mistakes: Writing that the union is permanent. The two cells separate after the exchange.
Writing that two ciliates of the SAME mating type conjugate. They must be of different mating types.
steps.memory_tip: Temporary union, different mating types, nuclear exchange: three conditions in one sentence.
steps.margin_note: One sentence, all three conditions. Do not describe the nuclear divisions.

steps.label: Result and examples
lines: After the exchange the two cells separate as
This restores the vigour and vitality of the
old cells. The number of individuals does not
increase, so conjugation is a sexual process
and not a method of reproduction.

lines.text: Conjugation: nuclear exchange, no new cells

steps.why: Two cells go in and two come out, so nothing has multiplied; what has changed is the nuclear material, and that is why the process renews an ageing ciliate instead of increasing the population.
common_mistakes: Calling conjugation a method of reproduction. The number of individuals stays the same.
Giving no examples. Two are asked for, and Paramecium alone is half the mark.
steps.memory_tip: Two in, two out: nothing is added, so it renews rather than reproduces.
steps.margin_note: The second mark needs BOTH examples written out.

insider_note: The question says give two examples, so Paramecium alone will not earn the second mark — write Vorticella beside it.
